title: Business Loan Sales Consultant / Closer — Warm Leads — AU Day Shift
description:
JOB OVERVIEW



Have you sold business loans, mortgages, asset finance or insurance? Bring your closing experience to Ezy Pzy Finance and help Australian business owners access funding.

We also welcome proven sales professionals from other industries who can demonstrate consistent target achievement and experience closing business over the phone.

You’ll receive warm enquiries, product training, weekly coaching and the opportunity to earn commission on both new and repeat clients.





YOUR EARNING OPPORTUNITY



•During probation: AUD $500/week + commissions + bonuses (approx. ₱97,500/month fixed base). After 8 weeks probation: AUD $650/week including PhilCare allowance + commissions (approx. ₱126,750/month fixed pay).

• Our agents currently average AUD $5,200/month (₱234,000/month) in total earnings including commissions and monthly bonuses.

• Earn between AUD $100 - $800 (approximately ₱4,500–₱36,000) commission per deal..

• Repeat business stays with you: when a client you funded returns for more funding, you handle their next deal and earn commission again.

• Earn additional monthly performance bonuses based on KPI’s achieved.

After your two-month probation, benefits include the base salary increase, an HMO allowance, paid annual and sick leave, and access to higher bonus tiers.





WHO WE ARE



Ezy Pzy Finance is a fast growing Australian business finance company connecting business owners with a panel of non-bank lenders.

We’re growing our remote sales team and looking for consultants who combine strong closing skills with clear communication and disciplined follow-up.

Learn more: 





WHAT YOU’LL DO



• Call Australian business owners who have already expressed interest in funding.

• Understand their business, funding needs and timing.

• Qualify enquiries and guide clients through the application process.

• Explain available options clearly, handle objections and move deals towards settlement.

• Keep your pipeline organised and follow up consistently.

• Build relationships that generate repeat business.



Warm leads are provided. There is no cold prospecting or list building, but the role involves regular outbound calls and persistent follow-up.





WHO SHOULD APPLY

title: Virtual Assistant – Automotive Auction Data Entry & Vehicle Research
description:
VIRTUAL ASSISTANT – AUTOMOTIVE AUCTION DATA ENTRY & VEHICLE RESEARCH



We are a car dealership looking for a reliable, detail-oriented Virtual Assistant to help with weekly vehicle auction research, vehicle valuation, and data entry.



WORK SCHEDULE



Monday–Friday, 10:00 AM–6:00 PM Central Time (Texas time).



You must be available and working during these hours. This is an ongoing, long-term position, not a one-time project.



MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES



You will review vehicles from multiple online automotive auction websites and enter the required information into our Google Sheets.



Your responsibilities will include:



• Review upcoming/pre-sale vehicle auction listings



• Enter vehicle information into our Google Sheets



• Record VIN, year, make, model, trim, mileage, auction location, and other required information



• Research vehicle market values using websites and tools we provide



• Enter estimated retail/market values



• Review post-sale auction results when required



• Record actual auction sale prices



• Match pre-sale and post-sale vehicles using VINs



• Compare auction prices with current vehicle values



• Follow our spreadsheet format exactly



• Check all work carefully for missing or incorrect information



• Complete assigned auction research and data entry by the required deadlines



REQUIREMENTS



We are looking for someone who:



• Has strong Excel and Google Sheets skills



• Is very comfortable with online research and data entry



• Has excellent attention to detail



• Can work efficiently with large amounts of vehicle data



• Understands basic vehicle information such as VIN, year, make, model, trim, and mileage



• Is dependable, consistent, and organized



• Can follow detailed instructions



• Can work Monday–Friday from 10:00 AM–6:00 PM Central Time



• Is interested in a long-term position



Automotive, dealership, or vehicle auction experience is preferred but not required.



TRAINING



We will provide training and instructions covering:



• The auction websites we use



• What vehicle information needs to be collected



• How to enter information into our Google Sheets



• Which websites and tools to use for vehicle values



• How our spreadsheets should be organized



• How to review pre-sale and post-sale auction information



Accuracy is extremely important. The information entered into our spreadsheets is used to help us make vehicle purchasing and bidding decisions.



TO APPLY



Please include:



• Your experience with Excel and Google Sheets



• Any automotive, dealership, auction, or vehicle research experience



• Confirmation that you can consistently work Monday–Friday from 10:00 AM–6:00 PM Central Time



• A brief description of similar data-entry or online research work you have done



IMPORTANT: Start your application with the words “CAR AUCTION” so we know you read the entire job posting.



We are looking for someone dependable who can become a long-term member of our team and become very familiar with our vehicle-buying and auction process.



ALSO PLEASE SEND US A 1 MINUTE VIDEO INTRODUCTION OF YOUR SELF

title: Full-Time WFH Customer Success and Retention Manager — $2,000 Base + Bonuses
description:
JOB OVERVIEW



Full-Time | Monday-Friday | PH Morning / US Evening Coverage



We are hiring Philippines-based Client Success Managers to support U.S. clients during evening hours, especially Pacific Time.



This is a client leadership role, not just support.



You will own the client relationship, keep clients clear and accountable, create momentum, prevent frustration, and escalate risks early.



This role is best for someone with excellent English, strong emotional intelligence, high ownership, and confidence handling high-ticket clients calmly.



Success is measured by retention, trust, communication, accountability, client momentum, and risk prevention.



SALARY



- Ramp / Trial CSM: USD 1,500/month base

- Certified CSM: USD 2,000/month base

- OTE: USD 2,500-3,000+/month with performance bonuses

- Paid twice a month via Wise

- Certification is performance-based, usually reviewed after 30-60 days, and requires consistent performance, quality-control review, and leadership approval



SCHEDULE



- Monday-Friday

- Full-time: 7.5 hours a day; 37.5 hours/week

- Core client coverage: 6 AM-12 PM PH time

- Split shifts are allowed

- Afternoons and early evenings are generally free

- Required team/training meetings may happen around 9 PM-11 PM PH time

- Occasional client calls may run up to 12 PM PH time when needed

- Final schedule will be agreed during hiring and must be sustainable long-term



ABOUT US



We help creators, beginners, coaches, and business owners grow and monetize online using short-form content, AI tools, strategy, coaching, and accountability.



We provide an “80% done-for-you” content and monetization system that helps clients turn short-form content into audience growth, leads, and income.



We have worked with 4,000+ clients since 2019.



Most clients are U.S.-based, and many are age 45+, so patience, clarity, emotional intelligence, and professional English communication are very important.



RESPONSIBILITIES



- Run client kickoff calls using our onboarding framework

- Set clear expectations from day one

- Help clients understand what to do next and why it matters

- Keep clients accountable to action items and deadlines

- Follow up with stuck, quiet, inactive, or delayed clients

- Re-engage clients before momentum is lost

- Respond to client messages within 24 weekday hours

- Close loops and avoid dangling threads

- Handle difficult conversations calmly and professionally

- De-escalate frustrated or emotional clients

- Identify refund, payment, chargeback, cancellation, and satisfaction risks early

- Escalate issues quickly according to SOPs

- Keep clear notes in Airtable / CRM

- Coordinate internally when support or escalation is needed

- Support renewals, referrals, testimonials, and upsell opportunities when appropriate

- Join required trainings, daily team Zoom calls, and feedback sessions

- Once activated, host a weekly client-support call or own a similar client-success responsibility



CLIENT LOAD



You will ramp gradually.



The target for a Certified CSM is 40-50 active clients, depending on client complexity, program type, and client inflow.



When fewer clients are available, CSMs may support reactivation, offboarding, client check-ins, and legacy-client cleanup.



BENEFITS



- Fully remote role

- Payment: Twice a month via Wise, always on time

- Performance-based bonuses

- Clear path from Ramp / Trial CSM to Certified CSM

- Growth opportunity into leadership

- Supportive international team

- Daily trainings and team Zoom calls

- SOPs, support, and structure provided

- Work with creators, brands, short-form content, and AI tools

- Required tools paid for after the test month where applicable

- Afternoons and early evenings generally free, with required evening meetings



REQUIREMENTS



- Currently based in the Philippines

- Fluent, professional English

- Clear and easily understood verbal communication

- Strong communication and emotional intelligence

- Calm under pressure

- High ownership, follow-through, and reliability

- Strong say-do ratio and respect for deadlines

- Comfortable handling difficult, emotional, or high-ticket clients

- Comfortable with uncomfortable conversations

- Strong Airtable / CRM documentation habits

- Reliable internet connection and professional home setup

- Willing to use Hubstaff during working hours

- Able to work PH morning / U.S. evening hours

- Comfortable with split shifts and required evening meetings

- Able to manage up to 40-50 active clients once trained and certified

- Able to meet certification standards without heavy supervision

- Able to identify and escalate refund, payment, chargeback, cancellation, and client-satisfaction risks quickly



NICE TO HAVE EXPERIENCE



- Client Success

- Account Management

- Coaching

- High-ticket programs

- Online education

- Social media monetization

- Content strategy

- Creator economy

- AI tools like ChatGPT, CapCut, or Submagic

- Working with U.S. clients



WE’RE THE RIGHT FIT IF



You’ll likely thrive here if you:



- Enjoy client-facing communication

- Stay calm when clients are emotional, frustrated, or confused

- Take ownership without needing to be micromanaged

- Follow through consistently and stay organized

- Want a long-term role with growth potential

- Can balance empathy with accountability

- Are comfortable working with U.S.-based clients



HOW TO APPLY



Apply here:



IMPORTANT: Put “CSM” + Your Full Name in the Name field.



P.S. Once hired, you will be contracted under Social Influence Consulting LLC.

title: Project Manager (Remote — Supporting U.S. Operations)
description:

Schedule: Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM CST (U.S.) 

Location: Remote 



 

About the Role 



We're hiring a Project Manager to take full ownership of a client project from kickoff through completion. This is not a task-only support role — you will be the person accountable for the project staying on schedule, the records staying accurate, and the client staying informed. 



You'll start with one project. That means you'll have the bandwidth to do it exceptionally well: running discovery and progress meetings with the client, scheduling and confirming appointments, coordinating technicians, chasing down loose ends, and giving leadership a clear, current picture of where things stand. 



We are building a team of high-performing professionals who think critically, move with urgency, and don't need to be told twice. 



 



What You'll Do 

-Project ownership 

-Own your project end to end: schedule, records, and on-time completion 

-Run discovery meetings and recurring progress meetings with clients 

-Coordinate with technicians to align availability, scope, and timing 

-Serve as the internal liaison, keeping the EST team on track with their deliverables 

-Build multi-state and multi-location deployment plans, and rework them when customer needs or resource availability shift 

-Anticipate delays and adjust timelines before they become problems 

-Build and send clear reports that give leadership a quick, accurate overview 



 



Scheduling and coordination 

-Heavy scheduling in Salesforce 

-Book and confirm client appointments by phone 

-Handle follow-up calls and
s through to resolution 

-Respond to
 promptly and professionally 



General administrative support 

-Records and accountability 

-Maintain accurate, current client records 

-Track deliverables, deadlines, and follow-ups without being reminded 

-Close the loop on every open item 



 



What We're Looking For 



A strong candidate can point to specific, concrete examples of the following: 

Project ownership — You've managed, coordinated, led, or owned projects from start to finish. Not assisted. Owned. 

Organization — You've juggled multiple projects, deadlines, priorities, and calendars at once and kept all of them straight. 

Communication — You've worked directly with clients, vendors, internal teams, and leadership, and you can speak and write clear, professional English. 

Problem solving — You've resolved issues, handled escalations, and adjusted timelines when reality didn't match the plan. 

Accountability — You've tracked deliverables, deadlines, KPIs, and follow-ups, and you owned the outcome, not just the activity. 

Remote experience — You've worked with remote or distributed teams and you're comfortable running virtual meetings on Teams, Slack, or Zoom. You do good work without someone watching over your shoulder. 

Client management — You've managed client communication, expectations, updates, and relationships directly. 

Tools — Experience with Salesforce, Asana, Monday, Jira, ClickUp, Trello, Teams, or Excel is a plus. We care less about which systems you've used than about how fast you pick up new ones. 

Career progression — Your work history shows increasing responsibility over time. 

Results — Your resume shows numbers and outcomes, not just a list of duties. Reduced delays, improved turnaround, managed X clients or projects — that's what we want to see. 



 



Requirements 

Fluent, professional spoken and written English 

Ability to think critically and make sound decisions without constant direction 

Ability to learn new systems quickly 

Ability to manage multiple responsibilities at once 

Full availability Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM CST. After training, your schedule may shift to 7:00 AM – 4:00 PM or 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM CST based on team needs. 

Your own computer and strong, reliable high-speed internet capable of clear VOIP calls

title: Bookkeeper — US Month-End Close Full Time (Remote)
description:
PLEASE READ THE INSTRUCTIONS PROPERLY FIRST===>



We provide monthly close services to US small businesses. Our production process is automated: transaction coding, bank and card matching, reconciliation, and recurring month-end entries are completed systematically, with an AI layer performing the initial categorisation before any file is assigned. We are hiring a bookkeeper to take ownership of the close on an assigned portfolio of client books.



This is not a conventional bookkeeping position. The seat does not involve coding a month from scratch or manual transaction entry. Files reach you with the mechanical work complete. Your responsibility begins where judgement is required: identifying what the automation has classified incorrectly, resolving what it could not determine, and establishing whether the month is accurate enough to release.



The position carries a second area of responsibility of equal weight: the accuracy of the automation itself on your portfolio. Where it consistently misclassifies a category, where a rule breaks and under what conditions, where it fails to identify something it should have. Establishing this is part of closing the month, and it determines how the system processes those files in subsequent periods.



Bookkeepers accustomed to performing every step personally generally do not find this arrangement satisfying. Bookkeepers who have spent years building out their own automation generally do.



Responsibilities

- Own the monthly close on an assigned portfolio, from automated draft through to delivery

- Review automated output in full and correct every misclassification before release

- Resolve edge cases and transactions the automation could not settle, including obtaining client clarification where required

- Prepare month-end entries outside the automated process: accruals, prepayments, depreciation, and client-specific adjustments

- Reconcile all accounts: bank, credit card, and balance sheet accounts with supporting documentation retained

- Deliver financial statements strictly to the agreed monthly schedule

- System feedback: Maintain a record of where the automation failed, the categories involved, and the time each correction required



Requirements

- Minimum five years of professional bookkeeping experience, of which at least the most recent two years have been on an automated workflow: bank feeds, rules, and at least one tool beyond the ledger itself. Both the total experience and the automation experience are required.

- Demonstrated expertise operating an automated bookkeeping stack. You configure and maintain bank rules rather than accept defaults, understand the conditions under which they break, and can state which transaction categories your software handles reliably and which require review without exception.

- Substantive hands-on use of AI within bookkeeping itself: classification, coding, document extraction, or transaction review, not correspondence or administrative tasks. You should be able to describe specific instances where an AI tool produced an incorrect result and how you identified it.

- Access to at least one closed month of books you are able to share for the practical assessment.

- Full monthly closes completed end-to-end for US, UK, or Australian clients.

- QuickBooks Online or Xero as your primary ledger.



What is NOT required:

- Certifications or accounting degrees



Not suitable for:

- Manual data entry roles or candidates who code a full month by hand

- Candidates whose experience is limited strictly to AP/AR or payroll without full month-end closes

- Candidates who have not worked on an automated bookkeeping stack



Schedule:

- Ability to work with direct overlap during US business hours (Night shift).



How to Apply:

- Do not apply/communicate here, fill the below form

- To be considered, you must complete our technical screening form.

- tally . so / r / pbp12B



Selection Process

- Application form (above link, ~5 minutes)

- A detailed questionnaire on your close process and how your tools behave, sent to those who qualify at stage two.

- Practical close assessment, extended to shortlisted candidates only. Runs on one closed month from your own books.

- Final Interview.



Note: All applications receive an outcome notification within 48 hours. Cover letters are not reviewed.



Benefits:

- Flexible schedule

- Flextime

- Opportunities for promotion

- Pay raise

- Work from home



Work Location: Remote

title: Short form editor for founder/vc
description:
About the role



I'm a venture capital investor based in London. I make short-form video about startups, funding, business strategy, culture and career, explainers, founder breakdowns, and a weekly series on who just raised money and why. The audience is smart, ambitious, mostly women, and allergic to fluff.



I film in batches once or twice a week: talking-head pieces to camera, walk-and-talk footage shot on a DJI Osmo Pocket, and screen recordings. I need an editor who can turn that raw footage into finished, ready-to-post verticals without me having to explain every time, so if you know a bit about tech and AI, have an interest, that would be great!!



This is a long-term working relationship, not a one-off gig. If it goes well, volume and pay both go up.



What you'll do

Edit 8–15 short-form videos per week (30–90 seconds each) from batch-filmed raw footage

Cut talking-head footage tightly for pace, remove filler, dead air, false starts, repeated takes, but also keep my style of editing

Write and time burned-in captions that are accurate to business and finance vocabulary (term sheet, Series A, valuation cap, down round, LP, dilution)

Add b-roll, screenshots, headlines, charts, text overlays, zooms and pattern interrupts so the first 3 seconds hold

Source relevant stock and screen-recorded b-roll where needed

Cut alternate versions of the same video for different hooks when I ask

Export clean 9:16 masters for TikTok and Instagram, plus cover/thumbnail frames

Keep files organised in Google Drive with clear naming, and track status in Notion

What I'm looking for

Real portfolio of vertical short-form work — TikTok or Reels, not YouTube long-form or wedding videos

Strong CapCut and/or Adobe Premiere Pro skills (After Effects a plus, not required)

Excellent written English comprehension. You'll be cutting dialogue for meaning, so you need to follow an argument and know where a sentence ends. Auto-captions full of misspelled finance terms are the fastest way to lose this job

Genuine familiarity with what's currently working on TikTok and Instagram trends, pacing, caption styles, hook structures

Reliable turnaround: first cut within 48 hours of receiving footage

Communicative. If something's unclear or the footage is unusable, tell me the same day, don't disappear

Able to take direct feedback and apply it across future edits without being told twice

Nice to have

Interest in business, startups, tech or finance

Experience editing for a personal brand or founder-led account

Motion graphics, animated text, simple data visualisation

Thumbnail and carousel design in Canva

Tools



CapCut or Premiere Pro, Google Drive, Notion, Canva. I'll provide brand fonts, colours and reference edits.



How to apply



Applications that ignore these steps will not be read.



Start your message with the word DILUTION so I know you read the whole post.

Send 2–3 links to vertical short-form videos you personally edited. Tell me what you did on each one — don't send agency reels where I can't tell what was yours.

In 3–4 sentences: what makes a talking-head video watchable past the first 5 seconds? Use an example.

title: Investor Relations & Marketing Assistant
description:
About Lynnfield



Lynnfield is a long-term holding company that buys and builds businesses that stand the test of time.



Over 3 million owners of profitable small businesses in the US are expected to retire over the next decade. 70% of them will fail because there is nobody to succeed the owner and there are not enough buyers to capture the opportunity. We are a partner to these owners, giving their companies a permanent home and preserving their legacy.



We fund these acquisitions with capital from family offices, high-net-worth individuals, and institutional credit and equity partners. We are building a community of investors who want exposure to profitable small businesses: people we educate first, build a real relationship with second, and invite into specific opportunities third. This role exists to build and run that engine.



Learn more at 



Role Overview



We're seeking an experienced assistant to run the day-to-day machinery of our investor relations and marketing. You'll work directly with our CEO, a serial entrepreneur who built and sold a manufacturing software company to a public acquirer, as the operating layer behind everything investor-facing.



This is a generalist role for someone who is good at several things at once: keeping a CRM immaculate, writing professional outreach, running social media, promoting events, and chasing down the details that make an executive look organized. We're looking for the person who ends up owning whatever needs owning.



You are the system. You grow and nurture our investor community, you keep the investor CRM accurate and current, you run our social presence, you draft and sequence the outreach that goes out under the CEO's name, you get him booked on the right podcasts, webinars, and conference stages, and you make sure every one of those appearances converts into a qualified relationship and a followed-up pipeline.



Our approach is patient and educational. We bring people into a community, teach them how passive investing in small businesses actually works, build genuine relationships over months, and then, once the relationship and the qualification are both real, the CEO discusses specific opportunities. Your job is to make that sequence run reliably at scale.



The right person is organized to the point of being a little obsessive, writes crisp professional English, and is comfortable operating inside the finance world. You'll be reading investor bios, capital provider websites, and conference attendee lists all day and d
 who matters.



Primary Responsibilities



Investor CRM & Pipeline Management (20%)



- Own our investor CRM as the single source of truth, with every contact, firm, check size, mandate, and interaction logged

- Research and enrich investor records: firm type (family office, RIA, fund of funds, private credit, independent-sponsor-focused equity), stated mandate, ticket size, prior deals, decision maker

- Administer our investor intake questionnaire, making sure every new community member completes it and that responses stay current in the CRM

- Build and maintain segmented lists by investor category, thesis fit, relationship stage, and qualification status

- Run the follow-up cadence so every warm contact gets a touch within the agreed window

- Maintain conference and event trackers (attendee lists, meeting requests sent, meetings booked, outcomes, next steps)

- Produce a weekly pipeline report: community growth, new qualified relationships, outreach sent, replies, meetings booked, stage movement



Investor Community Growth & Nurture (15%)



- Grow the Lynnfield investor community by driving qualified signups from events, appearances, outreach, and referrals

- Own the welcome and onboarding sequence for new members, including getting the intake questionnaire completed

- Run a consistent educational content cadence for the community: how passive investing in small businesses works, what makes a business acquirable, how deals get financed, what returns look like and why

-Write and send the regular investor newsletter, covering drafting, scheduling, segmentation, and performance reporting

-Segment communications so the right content reaches the right stage, with education for early members and depth for established relationships

-Track engagement at the individual level and flag warming relationships to the CEO for a personal conversation

-Keep the community content calendar full and shipping on schedule



Social Media & Digital Presence (20%)



- Own the day-to-day operation of the CEO's LinkedIn and the Lynnfield company page, our primary channels for reaching this audience

- Build and run the content calendar: plan themes, schedule posts, maintain a consistent publishing rhythm

- Draft posts in the CEO's voice on business acquisition, small business investing, deal-making, and entrepreneurship, including turning his rough voice notes and bullet points into finished posts

- Repurpose every podcast appearance, webinar, and talk into clips, quote graphics, carousels, and posts

- Manage engagement: respond to comments, monitor DMs and triage the ones that matter, engage thoughtfully on target investors' and partners' posts

- Grow followers and engagement among the audiences that matter: family offices, HNW investors, search fund and independent sponsor communities, business owners

- Produce simple graphics and short-form video edits for posts and event promotion at a Canva and CapCut level

- Track what performs and adjust, bringing us data on what the audience responds to



Outreach & Meeting Setting (20%)



- Draft personalized
 and LinkedIn outreach, sent under the CEO's name and from his accounts

- Frame outreach as an invitation into the investor community and its educational content

- Build multi-touch sequences that stay personal and individually researched

- Research each target before writing: recent deals, published theses, mutual connections, conference attendance

- Identify and prioritize new prospective investors from conference lists, industry databases, LinkedIn, podcasts, and press

- Manage the reply queue: triage responses, propose times, schedule meetings, send calendar invites and confirmations

- Prepare a short pre-meeting brief for every scheduled call covering who they are, what they fund, why they should care, and a suggested angle

- Send post-meeting follow-ups and materials, and log the outcome same-day



Speaking, Podcast & Conference Placement (15%)



- Build and maintain a target list of podcasts, webinars, conferences, and industry events where our audience shows up: family offices, HNW allocators, search fund and independent sponsor communities

- Pitch the CEO as a guest or speaker, which means researching the host, writing the pitch, sending it, following up, and tracking every submission

- Manage conference logistics: registration, speaker applications, CFP deadlines, meeting-scheduler systems, agenda building

- Maintain the speaker kit: bio variants, headshots, talk titles and abstracts, past appearances, one-sheet

- Track placements and keep a running library of appearances and links



Event & Webinar Promotion (10%)



- Promote every webinar, podcast appearance, and speaking slot through registration pages, invitation
s, LinkedIn posts, and reminder sequences

- Drive registration from our own investor list alongside the host's audience

- Coordinate with the host on co-promotion, assets, and audience sharing

- Handle post-event work: recordings, clips, recaps, and, most importantly, routing attendees and registrants into the investor community and the CRM with the right follow-up

- Track registration, attendance, and meeting conversion for every event



Required Qualifications



Essential Experience



5+ years supporting a founder or executive in some combination of investor relations, marketing, business development, executive assistance, or sales development, ideally at a financial services, investment, or B2B firm

CRM ownership. You have personally been responsible for the accuracy and hygiene of a CRM, and you can describe the system you kept it clean with.

Social media management. You have run a real business or executive account. Show us the accounts and what they looked like before and after you ran them.

US market experience. You have worked with US-based clients, companies, or audiences and understand US business norms.

Outbound outreach. You have written and sent personalized outreach that got replies from senior people, and you can show examples.

 and newsletter experience. You have built and run multi-stage nurture campaigns.

Research fluency. You can read a PE firm's website or an investor's LinkedIn and correctly summarize what they invest in.

Process discipline around rules. You have worked somewhere with real compliance constraints, and you follow the rule even when it's inconvenient.

Core Skills



Exceptional written English at native or near-native level, since you will be drafting in an executive's voice to sophisticated financial audiences

Genuine fluency with LinkedIn as a business platform, including a real sense of what performs there

Comfort producing simple visual content: graphics, quote cards, short video clips

Extreme organizational discipline, with everything tracked and everything logged

Comfort with financial vocabulary: EBITDA, capital stack, senior debt, mezzanine, equity co-invest, family office, accredited investor, LP

Self-directed, since you will get context and priorities and work out the steps yourself

Sound judgment about tone and timing, including knowing when to hold something back and ask

Available for 2 to 3 calls per week during US Pacific business hours (evening or early morning in your timezone) and responsive on Slack during agreed overlap hours

Highly Valued



Experience in private equity, search funds, independent sponsors, investment banking, or a family office

Experience booking executives on podcasts, panels, or speaking circuits

Familiarity with LinkedIn Sales Navigator and
 deliverability best practices

Experience with conference meeting-scheduler platforms such as MeetMax

Experience running an
 list, community, or membership program of any kind

Ghostwriting experience, meaning social content written in someone else's voice

Video editing for short-form clips using CapCut, Descript, or similar

Any exposure to securities marketing rules such as Reg D, accredited investor standards, and general solicitation. We will train, and familiarity is a real advantage.

Comfort building and maintaining trackers in Excel or Google Sheets

Work Environment & Tools



Setup:



Fully remote, flexible daily schedule, with required overlap for standing calls during US Pacific business hours

Part-time to start at 20 to 25 hours per week, with a path to more hours as the pipeline grows

Primarily asynchronous communication via Slack and

Tools You'll Use:



Investor CRM such as Attio or Airtable, with training provided

Google Workspace (Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Calendar)

LinkedIn and Sales Navigator

Social scheduling tools such as Buffer or Hootsuite

Canva and a short-form video editor

 sequencing and newsletter platforms

Webinar and event platforms such as Zoom or Luma

Slack for team communication

How We Measure Success



Investor community growth, measured as qualified new members per month with completed intake

CRM accuracy: every interaction logged, every relationship date and qualification status present and correct

Community engagement: newsletter open and click rates, content shipped on schedule

Social media: posting consistency, follower and engagement growth among target audiences, inbound conversations generated

Meetings booked per month with target investors

Speaking and podcast placements secured per quarter

Event registration and attendance numbers, and community signups generated from each event

Follow-up SLA: every warm reply handled same business day

Why This Role is Unique



Direct access. You work daily with the CEO.

Breadth. You'll build skills across investor relations, social media, content, events, and CRM operations.

Real exposure. You'll learn how acquisitions get financed, how family offices evaluate opportunities, and how private capital actually gets raised.

Visible impact. The meetings you book turn directly into the capital that buys companies.

Growth path. As the capital base grows, this role can expand into full-time investor relations leadership.

title: UX/UI Designer
description:
The UX/UI Designer plays a key role in creating intuitive, visually engaging, and conversion-focused digital experiences for e-commerce brands. This role requires a strong understanding of user-centered design, visual interface design, and online customer behavior across desktop and mobile platforms. The ideal candidate is creative, detail-oriented, and experienced in designing seamless shopping experiences that enhance usability, strengthen brand identity, and drive conversions. Experience designing for Shopify or other e-commerce platforms.

Knowledge of e-commerce best practices, including product page design, navigation, filtering, cart experience, and mobile optimization.

Excellent communication and collaboration skills.

This role is part of our passive recruitment efforts, and while an immediate opening may not be available, we welcome experienced and motivated candidates to express their interest. We look forward to connecting with you should a suitable opportunity arise.

title: INBOUND APPOINTMENT SETTER — HAIR SALON (WARM FACEBOOK/INSTAGRAM LEADS, $1,250–$2,000/MO OTE + 13TH MONTH PAY)
description:
READ THIS FIRST



We're hiring ONE full-time Inbound Appointment Setter to call warm leads from our
 and Instagram ad campaigns for a color-specialist hair salon in Fontana, California.



This is NOT cold calling. Every lead you speak to has already raised their hand by submitting their info through one of our ads. Your job is to reach them fast, build trust quickly, understand what they actually want, and guide them into a booked appointment.



This role demands two things at once: sharp conversational judgment AND tight process discipline. The conversations are where you win or lose the booking. The process — cadences, call dispositions, CRM hygiene, follow-up tasks — is what makes the whole system work and what lets us measure anything. You need both. People who are great at one and sloppy at the other don't last here.



On the conversation side, what we're really hiring for is the ability to think on your feet. Someone replies three days later with just "sorry, been busy." Someone says they want highlights but describes something else entirely. Someone says "that's a bit far for me" but what they really mean is they don't see why it's worth the drive. If you can read what people actually mean and move the conversation forward without being told what to say next, you'll do well here.



If you need to be spoon-fed a script for every situation, this won't work.



THIS IS A SALES ROLE. YOU NEED AT LEAST 6 MONTHS OF EXPERIENCE

PERSUADING PEOPLE AND MOVING THEM TOWARD A BOOKED APPOINTMENT

OR A SALE.



OTE: $1,250–$2,000/month (base $900–$1,000 + uncapped performance bonuses).

13th month pay included — paid every December, on top of your base. Not baked in. Not restructured. A full extra month of base pay, added on top.



---



ABOUT THE COMPANY



You'll be employed by Midnight Siren, a growth and client acquisition company that operates and supports beauty service businesses. Your day-to-day work focuses on a family-owned, color-specialist hair salon in Fontana, California that has served the Inland Empire for over 21 years.



The salon has 4.9 stars on Google with 200+ reviews and a stylist team with 75+ combined years of experience. The business is real, established, and respected in its market.



You'll work directly under Ethan, the founder of Midnight Siren — no middle managers, no agency layers between you and the person making decisions. The Midnight Siren team is small and tightly focused. The stylists at salon handle the in-salon experience; you and Ethan handle everything that gets a client booked.



A note on team structure: you will be the only appointment setter on the team. Your day-to-day working relationship is directly with Ethan. There are no peer-level coworkers, no team chat with other appointment setters, no group energy to feed off. If you thrive with autonomy, clear systems, and a direct manager relationship, this works well. If you need a team environment or peer social dynamic to stay motivated, this will feel isolating over time.



We're in an active scaling phase. Core processes exist and are being refined. They don't change daily, but they evolve as we learn. If you like improving systems alongside a team, you'll fit. If you want a fully crystallized corporate environment where nothing ever shifts, you won't.



---



WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY BE DOING



This is a front-line revenue role, not customer support.



Daily:



- Call new
/Instagram ad leads within minutes of opt-in (speed matters — you'll have task notifications throughout the day)

- Run our call script for the structured parts of the call, and use our frameworks + your own judgment for discovery and objection handling. The script covers the greeting, the offer, pricing, and the booking ask. Discovery can't be fully scripted — clients say what they say, and you'll need to adapt in real time.

- Respond to inbound SMS,
 
, and Instagram DMs that get escalated to a human when our AI can't handle them

- Collect cards on file via secure link (never over the phone), book appointments, reschedule, and cancel

- Call no-shows to get them back on the calendar

- Coordinate with stylists about client requests and scheduling needs

- Create follow-up tasks in HighLevel (our CRM)

- Submit a brief end-of-day report with your numbers



Weekly:



- One coaching/review call with Ethan (~30–45 min)

- Async coaching via Loom video reviews on your live call recordings between meetings

- Review your KPIs, own your numbers, and bring data-backed ideas to improve them



During training (first 2–4 weeks):



We'll meet daily for live coaching to get you fully ramped before transitioning to the weekly + async cadence.



---



A WORD ON THE CALL SCRIPT (READ CAREFULLY)



We use a script. We also need you to think.



Where the script is fixed: the greeting, how we introduce the salon, how we present the offer, how we state pricing, the booking ask, and our core objection responses. These are tested and they work. You run them as written. Your tone, warmth, and pacing are what make them sound human — not changing the words.



Where the script can't help you: everything a real client throws at you. A vague text with no context. A client describing a service using the wrong name. Someone who's hesitant but won't say why. Someone who asks about price before you've figured out what they actually want. There is no script for these. There's a framework, and there's your judgment.



This is the part people underestimate. A big chunk of this job is not reciting — it's listening to what someone actually means and figuring out the next move in seconds, while they're on the phone with you.



Scripts do change here, but only based on data. If you bring an idea for a better line, we'll A/B test it. If it wins, it becomes the script. What we don't do is let setters freelance changes on the fly, because then we can't measure what works.



If you want to be told exactly what to say in every situation, this role will frustrate you. If you like having strong structure AND room to think, you'll do well.



---



SCHEDULE (PACIFIC TIME — GRAVEYARD SHIFT IN PHILIPPINES)



All schedule references in this post are in US Pacific Time. Because PH is 15-16 hours ahead of California, each shift starts late at night your time and ends the following morning.

- US workdays: Monday through Friday

- US days off: Saturday and Sunday

- Hours per day: 8 hours of work + 1 hour of break (30 min lunch + 2× 15 min breaks, or 30 min lunch + 1× 30 min break — your call)

- Pacific Time (US): 7:45 AM – 4:45 PM PST



Philippine Time during US Standard Time (roughly November through mid-March):



Shift runs 11:45 PM – 8:45 AM PHT

- A US Monday shift = late Monday night through Tuesday morning your time

- A US Friday shift = late Friday night through Saturday morning your time

- Your days off in PH local time: Sunday and Monday (until your shift starts late Monday night)



Philippine Time during US Daylight Savings Time (roughly mid-March through early November):



- Shift runs 10:45 PM – 7:45 AM PHT

- Same day-shift logic as above — shift starts the previous calendar evening in PH



This schedule is FIXED. It's based on data showing when our booking demand peaks. If you need flexible hours, rotating shifts, or plan to hold another job during these times, this role is not a fit.

Please re-read this section carefully and make sure BOTH the standard-time and daylight-savings schedules work for you long-term before applying. The 1-hour shift twice a year is non-negotiable — it follows US business hours. Please make sure BOTH schedules work for you long-term before applying.



If you have never worked a graveyard shift before, think carefully before applying. We will ask you specifically how you plan to structure your sleep, and how you'll make the schedule work alongside your family or partner. "I'll figure it out" is not an answer that gets you hired. This shift is sustainable for people who plan for it and difficult for people who don't.



---



COMPENSATION



Base pay:



$900–$1,000/month (depending on experience), paid via Wise on the 1st and 15th of every month.



13TH MONTH PAY included — paid every December on top of your regular base, not restructured into it. Prorated in your first year if you start mid-year. Total annualized base compensation including 13th month: $11,700–$13,000.



Performance bonuses (uncapped, paid monthly):



- $3 per new client showed appointment

- $2 per existing client showed appointment

- $1 per rebooking confirmation (low-effort confirmation calls for clients who already booked through the salon)



Tiered cumulative threshold bonuses (paid monthly):



- +$75 at 90 showed appointments/month

- +$150 at 120 showed appointments/month

- +$350 at 150 showed appointments/month



Worked examples:



Baseline performer — 90 showed appointments/month:

- Base: $950 (midpoint)

- Performance: ~$225 (avg $2.50/show × 90)

- Threshold bonus: $75

- Total: ~$1,250/month



Solid performer — 120 showed appointments/month:

- Base: $950

- Performance: ~$300 (avg $2.50/show × 120)

- Threshold bonus: $225 ($75 + $150)

- Total: ~$1,475/month



Top performer — 150 showed appointments/month (90% show rate on ~167 booked):

- Base: $1,000

- Performance: $450 ($3×90 new + $2×20 existing + $1×40 rebooking)

- Threshold bonuses: $575 ($75 + $150 + $350)

- Total: ~$2,025/month



This is a PERFORMANCE-PAY ROLE. 30–50% of your monthly income should be earned through bonuses. The base is intentionally modest. If you want a high guaranteed salary with low expectations, this is not the role.



---



OTHER BENEFITS



1. Annual performance-based raise after your first year

2. 14 days of PTO per year, single bucket, available after 90-day probation (use for vacation, holidays, sickness — your call). For planned multi-day time off, give us at least 1 week's notice so we can plan coverage. Emergencies are understood — just communicate as soon as you can.

3. 90-day initial probation period. Pay is NOT REDUCED during probation.



To confirm you have read this post in full, include the word BURGUNDY in your answer to the final question on the application form



---



TARGET KPIs



- Lead to Booking Rate: 25%+

- Show Rate: 90%+

- Bookings per day: 4–9

- Showed appointments per month: 100–160

- Daily volume: Finish all assigned tasks each day. We supply ~17–25 leads per day plus follow-ups, no-shows, reactivations, and rebooking confirmations. HIGH CALL VOLUME (150–250 CALLS/DAY) IS NORMAL AND NON-NEGOTIABLE. If that sounds overwhelming instead of energizing, this is not a fit.



---



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR



Background:



- Female candidates tend to perform best with our 35–65 female clientele, so we especially encourage strong female applicants — but the role is open to all genders.

- Bilingual (English + Spanish) is a plus but not required.



Non-negotiable skills:



The five that matter most — these are what we screen hardest for:



- Real-time thinking. You generate a good response in seconds, not minutes. Under pressure, with no script in front of you. This is the single biggest predictor of success in this role.

- Inferential listening. You hear what someone means, not just what they said. A client says "I need to talk to my husband first" — she's usually not asking for permission, she's telling you something about price or certainty that she doesn't want to say directly. If you take everything at face value, you'll lose bookings.

- Conversational initiative. You never dead-end a conversation, and you don't give up on a lead that's still alive. A client says "that's kind of far for me" — a weak setter says "no problem, thanks anyway" and loses her. What she's actually telling you is that she doesn't believe the drive is worth it yet. That's not a rejection, it's an assumption you haven't disproven. Answering someone's question is only half a response; the other half is the move that keeps things going.

- Rapport building. You can get someone to open up and feel comfortable with you fast. This is the biggest factor in whether someone books. These are emotional decisions, not logical ones. You don't need American cultural references — you need to make people feel heard, understood, and safe.

- Diagnostic reframing. You can say someone's problem back to them more clearly than they said it. When you do that, people assume you have the solution. It's the fastest way to build trust that exists.



Everything else:



- ADVANCED ENGLISH WITH MINIMAL ACCENT. An American listener should not need to strain to understand you. If we have to focus to follow what you're saying, that's a disqualifier.

- STRONG SPOKEN COMMUNICATION — CLEAR, CONFIDENT VOICE. YOU DO NOT RAMBLE. YOU ARE NOT SOFT-SPOKEN. If you fill silence with words because dead air makes you nervous, this won't work.

- Typing speed: 40 wpm minimum (60+ strongly preferred). You'll be taking notes and sending texts while talking. You'll submit a typing test screenshot with your application.

- Process discipline. Every call gets dispositioned correctly. Every lead moves through the right cadence. Every opportunity gets marked accurately in the CRM. This isn't optional admin — it's how we measure everything. Great conversations with sloppy process still means we're flying blind.

- Script discipline for the structured parts of the call.

- Natural call control. You can guide a conversation efficiently without talking over clients or letting calls drift. You redirect politely and keep the call outcome-focused.

- Sales experience: 6 months minimum (1 year+ preferred). Job-hopping resumes (multiple roles under 3–6 months each) will be disqualified.

- Comfortable holding the line on policies (rescheduling, deposits, etc.) without weakening the script or over-promising.

- Objection handling — you acknowledge, ask questions to reframe, and guide the client. You don't fire off rebuttals that invoke more resistance.

- CRM literacy. GoHighLevel experience strongly preferred.

- High data accuracy. You enter info correctly the first time. This is a precision role, not a speed-only one.

- Strong working memory and multitasking — you can listen, think, type, recall rules, and follow scripts simultaneously without freezing.

- Emotional steadiness under high-volume periods. Spikes happen. You execute calm under load.



Preferred:



- Familiarity with the salon/beauty industry

- Personal interest in beauty or self-care

- Experience working with older female clientele (35–65)

- Experience with Slack, Slite, Airtable, Claude or ChatGPT (we use AI to streamline daily work — if you can leverage it, you'll move faster)



Mindset (MOST IMPORTANT):



We'd rather hire someone who's a 10 in mindset and 7 in sales skill than the reverse. Here's what we mean:



- Ownership & volume mindset — you take responsibility for outcomes, not tasks. You see high-volume, repetitive work as leverage, not burnout.

- Process discipline — you operate consistently inside defined systems. You let your personality show through tone and warmth, not by changing the words.

- Sales psychology — you understand how to influence through trust, value framing, and subtle urgency. You communicate with intention, not chit-chat.

- Speed bias — you move fast, close loops quickly, and accelerate under pressure instead of slowing down.

- Coachability — you receive feedback without ego and adapt immediately. No defensiveness, no excuses.

- KPI awareness — you understand the numbers behind your role and how your daily actions move them.



---



TECH REQUIREMENTS



Non-negotiable:



- Internet minimum requirements: 50 Mbps download, 10 Mbps upload, ping under 80ms. Stable connection. We will test your speed and audio live from your actual work setup before we hire.

- Backup plan for outages. If your internet or power cuts out mid-shift, you need a real fallback — mobile hotspot, secondary ISP, UPS, co-working space, or some combination. You'll describe your specific backup setup in your application.

- Computer: 8 GB RAM minimum (16+ preferred). Processor: Intel Core i5 or equivalent, 8th generation or newer. SSD preferred. Working laptop or desktop

- Mouse

- Wired headset with boom mic (3.5mm or USB-C). No Bluetooth, no laptop mic, no AirPods.

- Webcam — laptop built-in is fine. You'll be on camera for interviews, training, and coaching calls.

title: INBOUND APPOINTMENT SETTER — HAIR SALON (WARM FACEBOOK/INSTAGRAM LEADS, $1,250–$2,000/MO OTE + 13TH MONTH PAY)

OR A SALE.



OTE: $1,250–$2,000/month (base $900–$1,000 + uncapped performance bonuses).

13th month pay included — paid every December, on top of your base. Not baked in. Not restructured. A full extra month of base pay, added on top.



---

You'll be employed by Midnight Siren, a growth and client acquisition company that operates and supports beauty service businesses. Your day-to-day work focuses on a family-owned, color-specialist hair salon in Fontana, California that has served the Inland Empire for over 21 years.



The salon has 4.9 stars on Google with 200+ reviews and a stylist team with 75+ combined years of experience. The business is real, established, and respected in its market.



You'll work directly under Ethan, the founder of Midnight Siren — no middle managers, no agency layers between you and the person making decisions. The Midnight Siren team is small and tightly focused. The stylists at salon handle the in-salon experience; you and Ethan handle everything that gets a client booked.

There are no peer-level coworkers, no team chat with other appointment setters, no group energy to feed off. If you thrive with autonomy, clear systems, and a direct manager relationship, this works well. If you need a team environment or peer social dynamic to stay motivated, this will feel isolating over time.



We're in an active scaling phase. Core processes exist and are being refined. They don't change daily, but they evolve as we learn. If you like improving systems alongside a team, you'll fit. If you want a fully crystallized corporate environment where nothing ever shifts, you won't.



---



WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY BE DOING



This is a front-line revenue role, not customer support.



Daily:



- Call new
/Instagram ad leads within minutes of opt-in (speed matters — you'll have task notifications throughout the day)

- Run our call script for the structured parts of the call, and use our frameworks + your own judgment for discovery and objection handling. The script covers the greeting, the offer, pricing, and the booking ask. Discovery can't be fully scripted — clients say what they say, and you'll need to adapt in real time.

- Respond to inbound SMS,
 
, and Instagram DMs that get escalated to a human when our AI can't handle them

- Collect cards on file via secure link (never over the phone), book appointments, reschedule, and cancel

- Call no-shows to get them back on the calendar

- Coordinate with stylists about client requests and scheduling needs

- Create follow-up tasks in HighLevel (our CRM)

- Submit a brief end-of-day report with your numbers



Weekly:



- One coaching/review call with Ethan (~30–45 min)

- Async coaching via Loom video reviews on your live call recordings between meetings

- Review your KPIs, own your numbers, and bring data-backed ideas to improve them



During training (first 2–4 weeks):



We'll meet daily for live coaching to get you fully ramped before transitioning to the weekly + async cadence.



---



A WORD ON THE CALL SCRIPT (READ CAREFULLY)



We use a script. We also need you to think.



Where the script is fixed: the greeting, how we introduce the salon, how we present the offer, how we state pricing, the booking ask, and our core objection responses. These are tested and they work. You run them as written. Your tone, warmth, and pacing are what make them sound human — not changing the words.



Where the script can't help you: everything a real client throws at you. A vague text with no context. A client describing a service using the wrong name. Someone who's hesitant but won't say why. Someone who asks about price before you've figured out what they actually want. There is no script for these. There's a framework, and there's your judgment.

If you want to be told exactly what to say in every situation, this role will frustrate you. If you like having strong structure AND room to think, you'll do well.



---



SCHEDULE (PACIFIC TIME — GRAVEYARD SHIFT IN PHILIPPINES)



All schedule references in this post are in US Pacific Time. Because PH is 15-16 hours ahead of California, each shift starts late at night your time and ends the following morning.

- US workdays: Monday through Friday

- US days off: Saturday and Sunday

- Hours per day: 8 hours of work + 1 hour of break (30 min lunch + 2× 15 min breaks, or 30 min lunch + 1× 30 min break — your call)

- Pacific Time (US): 7:45 AM – 4:45 PM PST



Philippine Time during US Standard Time (roughly November through mid-March):



Shift runs 11:45 PM – 8:45 AM PHT

- A US Monday shift = late Monday night through Tuesday morning your time

- A US Friday shift = late Friday night through Saturday morning your time

- Your days off in PH local time: Sunday and Monday (until your shift starts late Monday night)



Philippine Time during US Daylight Savings Time (roughly mid-March through early November):



- Shift runs 10:45 PM – 7:45 AM PHT

- Same day-shift logic as above — shift starts the previous calendar evening in PH



This schedule is FIXED. It's based on data showing when our booking demand peaks. If you need flexible hours, rotating shifts, or plan to hold another job during these times, this role is not a fit.

Please re-read this section carefully and make sure BOTH the standard-time and daylight-savings schedules work for you long-term before applying. The 1-hour shift twice a year is non-negotiable — it follows US business hours. Please make sure BOTH schedules work for you long-term before applying.



If you have never worked a graveyard shift before, think carefully before applying. We will ask you specifically how you plan to structure your sleep, and how you'll make the schedule work alongside your family or partner. "I'll figure it out" is not an answer that gets you hired. This shift is sustainable for people who plan for it and difficult for people who don't.



---



COMPENSATION



Base pay:



$900–$1,000/month (depending on experience), paid via Wise on the 1st and 15th of every month.



13TH MONTH PAY included — paid every December on top of your regular base, not restructured into it. Prorated in your first year if you start mid-year. Total annualized base compensation including 13th month: $11,700–$13,000.



Performance bonuses (uncapped, paid monthly):



- $3 per new client showed appointment

- $2 per existing client showed appointment

- $1 per rebooking confirmation (low-effort confirmation calls for clients who already booked through the salon)



Tiered cumulative threshold bonuses (paid monthly):



- +$75 at 90 showed appointments/month

- +$150 at 120 showed appointments/month

- +$350 at 150 showed appointments/month



Worked examples:



Baseline performer — 90 showed appointments/month:

- Base: $950 (midpoint)

- Performance: ~$225 (avg $2.50/show × 90)

- Threshold bonus: $75

- Total: ~$1,250/month



Solid performer — 120 showed appointments/month:

- Base: $950

- Performance: ~$300 (avg $2.50/show × 120)

- Threshold bonus: $225 ($75 + $150)

- Total: ~$1,475/month



Top performer — 150 showed appointments/month (90% show rate on ~167 booked):

- Base: $1,000

- Performance: $450 ($3×90 new + $2×20 existing + $1×40 rebooking)

- Threshold bonuses: $575 ($75 + $150 + $350)

- Total: ~$2,025/month



This is a PERFORMANCE-PAY ROLE. 30–50% of your monthly income should be earned through bonuses. The base is intentionally modest. If you want a high guaranteed salary with low expectations, this is not the role.



---

1. Annual performance-based raise after your first year

2. 14 days of PTO per year, single bucket, available after 90-day probation (use for vacation, holidays, sickness — your call). For planned multi-day time off, give us at least 1 week's notice so we can plan coverage. Emergencies are understood — just communicate as soon as you can.

3. 90-day initial probation period. Pay is NOT REDUCED during probation.



To confirm you have read this post in full, include the word BURGUNDY in your answer to the final question on the application form

- Lead to Booking Rate: 25%+

- Show Rate: 90%+

- Bookings per day: 4–9

- Showed appointments per month: 100–160

- Daily volume: Finish all assigned tasks each day. We supply ~17–25 leads per day plus follow-ups, no-shows, reactivations, and rebooking confirmations. HIGH CALL VOLUME (150–250 CALLS/DAY) IS NORMAL AND NON-NEGOTIABLE. If that sounds overwhelming instead of energizing, this is not a fit.



---



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR



Background:



- Female candidates tend to perform best with our 35–65 female clientele, so we especially encourage strong female applicants — but the role is open to all genders.

- Bilingual (English + Spanish) is a plus but not required.



Non-negotiable skills:



The five that matter most — these are what we screen hardest for:



- Real-time thinking. You generate a good response in seconds, not minutes. Under pressure, with no script in front of you. This is the single biggest predictor of success in this role.

- Inferential listening. You hear what someone means, not just what they said. A client says "I need to talk to my husband first" — she's usually not asking for permission, she's telling you something about price or certainty that she doesn't want to say directly. If you take everything at face value, you'll lose bookings.

- Conversational initiative. You never dead-end a conversation, and you don't give up on a lead that's still alive. A client says "that's kind of far for me" — a weak setter says "no problem, thanks anyway" and loses her. What she's actually telling you is that she doesn't believe the drive is worth it yet. That's not a rejection, it's an assumption you haven't disproven. Answering someone's question is only half a response; the other half is the move that keeps things going.

- Rapport building. You can get someone to open up and feel comfortable with you fast. This is the biggest factor in whether someone books. These are emotional decisions, not logical ones. You don't need American cultural references — you need to make people feel heard, understood, and safe.

- Diagnostic reframing. You can say someone's problem back to them more clearly than they said it. When you do that, people assume you have the solution. It's the fastest way to build trust that exists.

OTE: $1,250–$2,000/month (base $900–$1,000 + uncapped performance bonuses).

title: Manager, Billing & Financial Operations - Remote
description:
Company Overview



The Compliance Services Organization didn't exist. We built it.



MedPro Disposal is the nation's largest privately-held medical waste company, serving 35,000+ healthcare providers across 48 states for the past 15 years. On that foundation, we launched MP1 Solutions to pioneer the Compliance Services Organization (CSO) — a new category of operating partner built to replace the fragmented vendor model that has defined healthcare compliance for decades. MP1 Solutions extends MedPro Disposal's operational infrastructure, vendor network, and customer trust into a category we're actively building — and leading — with a technology-forward approach that's making this model smarter, faster, and more scalable as we grow.



What we do: We operate as the single compliance partner for non-acute healthcare facilities — consolidating every obligation into one coordinated program, assigning one dedicated account manager as the point of accountability, and actively managing the underlying vendor ecosystem through continuous evaluation, negotiation, and optimization on the practice's behalf.



Why it matters: Regulated facilities across the country are managing compliance the same fragmented way they always have. We're changing that, backed by 15 years of MedPro Disposal's operational credibility — and we're looking for people who want to help build what comes next.



Our technology: We're actively building the AI infrastructure that sits behind this model — automating compliance tracking, surfacing risks before they become problems, and creating a system that gets smarter with every client we add. If you want to build at the intersection of compliance and technology, you're in the right place.



Our impact: Our clients never have to worry about something falling through the cracks — obligations are coordinated, tracked, and documented in one place. We audit costs, eliminate overcharges, and deliver proof of compliance that always keeps practices inspection ready. Every client has one dedicated account manager who owns their program end to end. And unlike a traditional vendor relationship, our model is designed to get better over time — continuously re-evaluated, optimized, and improved with every client we serve.



Position Overview:

The Manager, Billing & Financial Operations is the operational owner of MedPro Disposal and MP1 Solutions' non-CA financial transaction engine — the function that ensures every invoice goes out accurately, every payment gets applied, every vendor gets paid, and every manifest and billing record is reconciled and audit-ready.



This is a 1st-line management role for a detail-obsessed, process-driven leader who has run billing and collections teams before. You are not just doing the work — you are building the systems, the SOPs, and the team discipline that make the work run without constant supervision. You manage the specialists; you own the numbers; you report up to leadership with clean, confident data.



Key Responsibilities:

Billing Operations & Transaction Processing

• Own end-to-end billing operations — from invoice generation through delivery, dispute resolution, and closed-loop reconciliation across all MedPro and MP1 service lines

• Oversee accurate and timely processing of all financial transactions: vendor payables, service billings, manifest entries, client invoices, and payment applications

• Ensure all billing records align with service agreements, contracts, and pricing structures — identifying and correcting discrepancies before they reach the client or vendor

• Manage the billing cycle calendar: maintain a disciplined, predictable cadence for invoice runs, payment postings, and month-end closes

title: AI UGC Video Editor (Google VEO Flow + CapCut) - 7 videos/day, long-term
description:
I'm looking for someone who ALREADY knows how to make AI UGC videos, not someone who wants to learn from scratch.



I've attached an example video. This is exactly the style and quality level I need. Watch it before you apply.



THE WORKLOAD

7 finished product videos per day, each 1 to 2 minutes long. That's the job. It's real volume and I want you to know that before you apply.



It's doable because the process is systemized. I send you the script, the reference video, the character reference image and the exact prompts the day before, so you have the full day to work. You're not inventing anything from scratch.



Week 1 is 5 to 6 a day while I audit your workflow with you and help you get faster. After that it's 7.



If you can only do 3 to 4 a day at good quality, tell me honestly in your application. I'd rather know now than find out in week two.



WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

- Generating AI avatars / AI characters that talk (Google VEO Flow)

- Assembling everything in CapCut: cuts, captions, timing, subtle background music

- Recreating a reference video closely while swapping in my avatar, my pet, my product and my setting

- Checking every clip before it goes in, no broken generations, no bad lip sync

- Exporting vertical 9:16, 1080x1920 MP4 and uploading them one by one as you finish



THE 8 THINGS I GET TIRED OF FIXING

This is the real job description. These are the notes I end up sending editors over and over. If you already do these without being told, you will do very well here.



1. Character consistency. Every video has a character reference image. The face, the outfit, the pet and the setting stay the same across every clip and across every video that character appears in. Don't redesign the character, don't let the face drift between clips.



2. Voice consistency. One voice start to finish. No echo, no reverb, no accent that shows up halfway through the video and disappears again. Rewatch the whole thing with headphones before you send it. If one scene has an accent or an echo, regenerate that scene.



3. Lip sync. If it's off by half a second, regenerate it. I notice.



4. Captions. Always on, clean, synced and styled like the reference video. "Missing captions" should never be a note I have to send you.



5. Background music. Subtle, sitting under the voice, matching the reference, and stopping where the reference stops it. Not missing, not blasting over the dialogue.



6. Match the reference. When I say copy it 1 to 1, I mean the framing, the pacing, the energy and the shot order. The avatar should fill the frame the way the reference does, not sit small in the middle. Natural phone footage look, not a cinematic color grade. And use MY background and setting, not the one from the inspo video.



7. Export quality. Download 720p from Flow, export from CapCut with the settings I give you, vertical 9:16 1080x1920. No blurry clips, no clips where the quality obviously jumps mid-video, no watermarks.



8. Revisions get done the same day. When I send a fix, it gets fixed that day, it doesn't get stacked onto next week. Keep your Flow generations and your CapCut project file so a small fix stays a small fix instead of a full rebuild.



FLOW CREDIT DISCIPLINE (matters as much as the editing)

- Images cost 0 credits. Perfect the image first, then generate the video.

- One clip generation per scene. Never x2, x3 or x4.

- Never 16:9. Everything is vertical.

- Every video generation costs credits whether it comes out good or bad. There are no refunds for a bad clip, so the prompt has to be right before you hit generate.

- Screenshot the credit balance when you start and when you finish each assignment.



I provide the accounts and the credits. Burning through them carelessly is the fastest way off the team.



REQUIREMENTS (please read, I skip applications that ignore this)

1. You MUST send me examples of AI videos you've personally made. Links to the actual videos, not a resume, not a portfolio site with stock work. If you've made something close to my example video, lead with that one.



2. Be ready to prove the work is yours. I get sent the same recycled portfolio folders by different people every week. I may ask for a bigger folder from that client, a project file, or a short screen recording of your workflow. If you can't show that, don't apply.



3. Real CapCut experience. Captions, keyframes, audio ducking, speed ramps, without me explaining them.



4. Hands-on experience with at least one AI video tool (Google VEO / Flow, Kling, Higgsfield, HeyGen, Sora, etc). Tell me which ones and what you used them for.



5. Consistency. Same hours, same days, every week, Saturdays included. This is an ongoing long-term role, not a one-off project. There's a 3 strike system: a missed day with no message ahead of time is a strike, and repeating the same mistake after I've given you feedback is a strike.



6. A computer that can actually handle exporting 7 videos a day without crashing, and reliable internet.



NICE TO HAVE

- You watch short-form content and have opinions on why some hooks work

- Experience with UGC / DTC ads, supplements, skincare or pet products

- Basic understanding of ad compliance (no medical claims, no "cures")



HOW TO APPLY

Start your message with the word "FLOW" so I know you read the whole post. Then:

1. Link 1 to 3 AI videos you made yourself. Say what you did on each one.

2. Tell me which AI video tools you've used.

3. Tell me honestly: how many 1 to 2 minute videos can you finish in one day at the quality level of my example video?

4. Tell me your working hours and which days you can commit to.

5. Pick one thing from the list of 8 above and tell me how you personally avoid it.



Applications without example videos will not get a reply.



WHAT YOU GET FROM ME

- Scripts, reference videos, character reference images and prompts for every single video, sent the day before, no guessing

- Full training on my exact process and prompt library, plus Loom feedback on your work

- Accounts and credits provided

- A predictable daily routine, not chaotic requests

- Long-term stable work with a raise as you get faster and better, plus a bonus at the end of the month based on performance

WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS

Most of how we find leads, source properties, and coordinate move-ins already runs on automation. But the moment a landlord needs reassurance before renting to a corporate housing company, or a traveling client needs to hear a real voice before they commit, that's a conversation, not a workflow. We need someone who can pick up the phone, build trust fast, and close.



ABOUT US

Trident Corporate Housing places corporate travelers, relocating employees, and traveling professional crews into fully furnished homes across the U.S., working directly with independent landlords to build a flexible, professional housing network.



ABOUT THE ROLE

You'll be the primary voice our landlords and clients hear on the phone, the person they trust enough to close a deal with in one or two conversations. You'll own the calls that actually convert: pitching our leasing model to landlords, running discovery calls with prospective clients, and following up until a lead either books or falls out of the pipeline.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Call landlords on properties our sourcing team has identified, pitch our leasing model, and screen them for fit

- Host discovery/intro calls on Google Meet when a lead needs more information before committing

- Negotiate rate and terms with landlords to protect margin while keeping the property competitive

- Follow up consistently on open leads until they convert or are disqualified

- Log every call outcome, objection, and next step in our CRM

- Hand off confirmed bookings cleanly to the operations team for move-in coordination



REQUIRED

- 2+ years of experience in outbound sales, phone-based customer service, real estate leasing, or a similarly phone-heavy sales role

- Excellent spoken English with clear, easy-to-understand pronunciation

- Comfortable making cold and warm calls, and confident handling objections

- Reliable high-speed internet, a quiet workspace, and a professional headset

- Available to work U.S. business hours (approx. 9am-6pm Eastern, Monday-Friday)



PREFERRED

- Experience in real estate, property management, corporate housing, or short/mid-term rentals

- Experience using a CRM to track calls and pipeline

- Comfortable on Google Meet/Zoom for client-facing video calls



COMPENSATION

$4-$6/hour USD, based on experience. Full-time, long-term contractor role with room to grow as we scale the team.



HOW TO APPLY

Apply with your resume AND a short (60-90 second) voice or video recording introducing yourself and describing a time you closed a sale or resolved a tough customer call. Applications without the recording will not be considered.
